claims.evidence: StatPearls: pelvis consists of right and left hip bones with the midline sacrum and coccyx; OpenStax says the same.
StatPearls Pelvis Bones: links spine and lower limbs; Pelvic Bones: carries trunk load down into the legs during standing and walking.
claims.newSentence: It links the spine and the lower limbs, and it carries the weight of the trunk down to the legs during standing and walking.

claims.evidence: StatPearls: rigid bony ring shields organs inside it; names bladder, rectum, female reproductive organs housed there; Pelvis page lists internal reproductive organs.
claims.newSentence: The pelvic cavity inside the bony ring houses the urinary bladder, rectum and internal reproductive organs, which the pelvis helps to protect.

claims.evidence: StatPearls Pelvis Bones: right and left hip bones together with midline sacrum and coccyx; OpenStax agrees.
OpenStax: each adult hip bone is formed by three separate bones that fuse together during the late teenage years. StatPearls timing vaguer (see notes).
Pelvic Joints page covers sacroiliac and sacrococcygeal joints; hip bones join at pubic symphysis; Pelvis Bones lists four pelvic joints. Front/back are standard directions.
OpenStax key terms: greater pelvis is broad upper region above pelvic brim, lesser pelvis narrow lower region; StatPearls inlet: true pelvis below, false above.
OpenStax 8.3 names iliac crest, ischial spine, ischial tuberosity, obturator foramen and acetabulum as hip bone landmarks.
OpenStax review: supports upper body, transfers weight to lower limbs; StatPearls: carries trunk load to legs and its rigid bony ring shields organs inside.
CT assessing pelvic anatomy and detecting bleeding is in StatPearls Pelvic Fracture; X-ray for pelvic injury was not stated in retrieved text.
claims.newSentence: CT helps to assess the pelvis and detect bleeding after injury

claims.evidence: OpenStax: coxal bone is one of two bones that with sacrum and coccyx make up the pelvis; 'single bone' wording and spine link not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: The hip bone, also called the coxal bone, is one of two bones that together with the sacrum and coccyx make up the pelvis.

claims.evidence: OpenStax: 'Each adult hip bone is formed by three separate bones that fuse together during the late teenage years.'
claims.newSentence: Each adult hip bone is formed by three separate bones, the ilium, ischium and pubis, that fuse together during the late teenage years.

claims.evidence: OpenStax: upper, fan-shaped part, curved superior margin is iliac crest; StatPearls Bones (Ilium, Ischium, Pubis): ilium physically largest of the three.
OpenStax: large roughened inferior ischium is the ischial tuberosity, carrying body weight when sitting; StatPearls: ischium is posteroinferior.
OpenStax: pubis is the anterior part and curves medially to join the opposite pubis at the pubic symphysis.
OpenStax: three areas converge to form a deep, cup-shaped cavity, the acetabulum, on the lateral side, part of the hip joint.
claims.newSentence: The three bones converge to form the acetabulum, a deep, cup-shaped cavity on the lateral side of each hip bone that is part of the hip joint.

claims.evidence: OpenStax: crest ends at the rounded anterior superior and the posterior superior iliac spines; inferior spines lie below. 'Rounded' AIIS, 'curves downwards' not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: The iliac crest ends at the rounded anterior superior iliac spine in front and the posterior superior iliac spine behind, and the anterior inferior and posterior inferior iliac spines lie below them.

claims.evidence: OpenStax: U-shaped greater sciatic notch lies superior to the ischial spine, the bony projection separating it from the lesser notch; 'pointed' not stated.
claims.newSentence: On the posterior margin of the ilium the greater sciatic notch, a large U-shaped indentation, lies above the ischial spine, the bony projection that separates it from the lesser sciatic notch.

claims.evidence: OpenStax: 'The large anterior opening is the obturator foramen', between the ischium and pubis; 'lower front' not stated.
claims.newSentence: The obturator foramen is the large opening at the front of the hip bone, between the ischium and pubis.

claims.evidence: OpenStax: ischial tuberosity is the attachment for the posterior thigh muscles. StatPearls excerpts gave no hamstring or pelvic-floor-on-pubis attachment; those clauses removed.
claims.newSentence: The ischial tuberosity also serves as the attachment for the posterior thigh muscles.

claims.evidence: StatPearls: pelvis is the hip bones together with the midline sacrum and coccyx; wording unchanged.
StatPearls: os coxae join at the pubic symphysis; interosseous sacroiliac ligament is the main sacrum-ilium connection; OpenStax: pubic symphysis joins the two pubes.
Sacrococcygeal joint is named on the Pelvic Joints page but the coccyx-sacrum attachment is not stated in excerpts; standard anatomy.
StatPearls excerpts: interosseous sacroiliac ligament is the main sacrum-ilium connection; anterior, posterior and interosseous ligaments each contribute to stabilisation (see notes).
claims.newSentence: The anterior, posterior and interosseous sacroiliac ligaments each contribute to stabilising the sacroiliac joint, and the interosseous ligament forms the main connection between the sacrum and ilium.

claims.evidence: Pelvic Joints: the sacroiliac joint is supplied by several vessels, including the iliolumbar, superior gluteal and lateral sacral arteries.
Excerpts gave only ligament roles (limiting ilium movement), not attachments; the origins and insertions stated are standard anatomy.
StatPearls: sacrotuberous and sacrospinous ligaments form the greater and lesser sciatic foramina; pudendal nerve lies between them. 'Vessels' not stated.
claims.newSentence: Together these two ligaments form the greater and lesser sciatic foramina, and the pudendal nerve lies between them.

claims.evidence: StatPearls Pelvic Inlet: limit between true pelvis inferiorly and false pelvis superiorly; OpenStax: brim, also called inlet, divides greater and lesser regions.
Supported: brim begins at sacral promontory and pubic symphysis; OpenStax lists pectineal and arcuate lines. Iliopectineal line, sacral ala and line-to-bone attributions not retrieved.
claims.newSentence: It begins at the sacral promontory behind and the pubic symphysis in front, and its boundary landmarks also include the pectineal and arcuate lines.

claims.evidence: StatPearls: wings of the ilium above the line form the greater (false) pelvis, which is part of the abdomen; OpenStax: broad upper region.
StatPearls Pelvic Outlet: lower margin of true pelvis, bounded by coccyx, ischial tuberosities and pubic symphysis; OpenStax: lesser pelvis is the narrow lower region.
StatPearls: below the brim lie bladder, rectum and part of the descending colon; true pelvis holds colon, internal reproductive organs, uterus, tubes, ovaries. 'Colon' used.
claims.newSentence: The true pelvis holds the urinary bladder, rectum and part of the colon, and also the uterus, fallopian tubes and ovaries in people who have them.

claims.evidence: Excerpts said female inlet is 'rounder or oval'; male 'heart-shaped' was not retrieved, so sentence removed (rounder-inlet fact kept in c34).
OpenStax: female sacrum wider, shorter, less curved; promontory juts less into the pelvic cavity, giving the female inlet a rounder or oval outline.
claims.newSentence: The female sacrum is described as wider, shorter and less curved, with a sacral promontory that projects less into the pelvic cavity, which gives the inlet a rounder or oval outline.

claims.evidence: OpenStax figure caption: female pelvis has a larger subpubic angle, a rounder pelvic brim and a wider, shallower lesser pelvic cavity. Male wording dropped.
claims.newSentence: It describes the female pelvis as having a larger subpubic angle, a rounder pelvic brim and a wider, shallower lesser pelvic cavity.

claims.evidence: OpenStax review: female pelvis has broader greater sciatic notch; male pelvic bones 'thicker and heavier'. Male notch 'deeper' not stated.
claims.newSentence: The greater sciatic notch is described as broader in the female pelvis, and in general the bones of the male pelvis are thicker and heavier.

claims.evidence: OpenStax review: 'Compared to the male, the female pelvis is wider to accommodate childbirth'; section 8.3 table gives general differences.
claims.newSentence: OpenStax describes general differences between the female and male pelvis, and says the female pelvis is wider to accommodate childbirth.

claims.evidence: OpenStax review: the pelvic girdle's main role is to support the upper body and transfer body weight to the lower limbs.
claims.newSentence: The main role of the pelvic girdle is to support the upper body and transfer body weight to the lower limbs.

claims.evidence: StatPearls: links spine and lower limbs during locomotion; passage for neurovascular structures. Supported, but removed as duplicate of intro to limit length.
Bone Markings: hip bone 'forms a sturdy basin that supports the trunk and provides attachment for lower limb muscles and ligaments'; draft's 'each' dropped.
claims.newSentence: StatPearls describes the hip bone as forming a sturdy basin that supports the trunk and provides attachment for lower limb muscles and ligaments.

claims.evidence: StatPearls: rigid bony ring shields the organs inside it. Supported, but removed as duplicate of intro; 'abdominopelvic' not retrieved.
StatPearls Pelvic Outlet: in females, the outlet offers support and guidance for a fetus through the birth canal.
claims.newSentence: In females, the pelvic outlet also offers support and guidance for a foetus through the birth canal.

claims.evidence: StatPearls: anterior division feeds pelvic organs, perineum, gluteal and adductor areas; posterior division supplies parietal pelvic structures and gluteal region (iliolumbar, lateral sacral, superior gluteal).
claims.newSentence: The internal iliac artery divides into anterior and posterior divisions: the anterior supplies the pelvic organs, the perineum and the gluteal and adductor areas, and the posterior supplies the parietal structures of the pelvis and the gluteal region.

claims.evidence: Frimley: fall from standing most often; falls common in older people; osteoporosis can weaken bones. Plymouth: more prone if bones thin.
claims.newSentence: A fracture of the pubic rami, which are parts of the pubis at the front of the pelvis, most often follows a fall from standing. Falls are common in older people, and people are more prone to these fractures if their bones are thin (osteoporosis).

claims.evidence: Frimley: pain usually increases with movement and weight bearing; fractures usually need no surgery (conservative). Plymouth: normally treated conservatively.
claims.newSentence: A Frimley Health NHS leaflet says that pain usually increases with movement and weight bearing, and NHS trust leaflets say that these fractures are usually managed without surgery.

claims.evidence: Pelvic Ring Injuries: names the posterior pelvic venous plexus as the main (leading) source of bleeding in pelvic ring injuries.
NHS: breaks in the top of the thigh bone near the hip joint, usually from a fall or injury to the side of the hip.
claims.newSentence: A hip fracture is a different injury, a break in the top of the thigh bone close to the hip joint, usually caused by a fall or an injury to the side of the hip.

claims.evidence: Healthier Together: PGP is 'uncomfortable symptoms caused by a stiffness of your pelvic joints or the joints moving unevenly' at back or front of pelvis.
claims.newSentence: Healthier Together, an NHS Wales site, describes pelvic girdle pain in pregnancy as a collection of uncomfortable symptoms caused by stiffness of the pelvic joints, or the joints moving unevenly, at the back or front of the pelvis.

claims.evidence: NHS and South Tees: pain over pubic bone and lower back; NHS: spreads to thighs; speak to midwife or GP if moving is hard.
claims.newSentence: Pain can be felt over the pubic bone at the front and across one or both sides of the lower back, and it can spread into the thighs. The NHS advises speaking to a midwife or GP if pelvic pain makes it hard to move around.

claims.evidence: NHS: imaging (X-ray, MRI or CT) confirms a fracture. Worcestershire trust leaflet: suspected from symptoms, examination, history; confirmed by X-ray or occasionally CT.
claims.newSentence: A hip fracture is usually first suspected from the symptoms, a physical examination and the history of the injury, and imaging such as an X-ray, an MRI scan or a CT scan is used to confirm it.

claims.evidence: StatPearls: CT helps assess pelvic anatomy and detect bleeding; do not assume ring injury is the only bleeding source; exclude thoracic and abdominal bleeding first.
claims.newSentence: For pelvic injuries, StatPearls notes that CT helps to assess the pelvis and detect bleeding, and cautions clinicians not to assume that a pelvic ring injury is the only source of bleeding, with chest and abdominal bleeding excluded first.

claims.evidence: Northampton: 'You won't feel anything during the exposure'; keep still so image isn't blurred; several X-rays from different angles; procedure usually takes a few minutes.
claims.newSentence: An X-ray examination usually takes only a few minutes and nothing is felt during the exposure; the person needs to keep still so that the image is not blurred, and several X-rays may be taken from different angles.

notes: 1) Search tool: allowed_domains ['www.nhs.uk'] returned no NHS pages (one search wasted); ['nhs.uk'] works. 2) 'Basin' sentence: StatPearls Bone Markings does say the hip bone 'forms a sturdy basin that supports the trunk', but one hip bone is only part of the basin, so 'each' was dropped and the wording is attributed to StatPearls. 3) c11: the draft's 'single bone that makes up the pelvic girdle' was not in retrieved text and reads as one bone in total; replaced with OpenStax's 'one of two bones' wording. 4) 'Late teenage years' fusion is OpenStax's wording; a StatPearls excerpt placed completion of pelvic development later (about 25 years), so a clinician may prefer softer wording. 5) Shape comparisons: only retrieved OpenStax wording kept; the male 'heart-shaped' inlet and male 'narrower and deeper' notch and lesser pelvis were not retrieved and were removed. 6) Internal iliac artery: the draft sentence had no support on the Pelvis page; a second query found the anterior and posterior division territories on StatPearls Internal Iliac Arteries and the sentence was rewritten from that. 7) Same-publisher attribution caveats: c24 ('each contribute to stabilisation') was indexed to another StatPearls page (Sacral Vertebrae, NBK551653), not the cited joint pages; c13 ('ilium largest') came from an NCBI excerpt not tied to one page, with the Ilium, Ischium and Pubis page in the result list. Worth a glance. 8) Pubic rami: Frimley leaflet is dated 1 April 2026, but the Plymouth leaflet shows a March 2021 review date (past) and some South Tees pages were flagged as over three years old; they are corroboration only. The clause 'pubic rami are parts of the pubis at the front of the pelvis' in c44 is textbook (not retrieved). 9) PGP: the owner of the Healthier Together page is not named in retrieved text, so the reference is retitled 'Healthier Together (NHS Wales)'; it says PGP is 'caused by' joint stiffness or uneven movement, whereas nhs.uk says the cause is 'thought to be linked to' several issues; 'hips and groin' were dropped as unconfirmed on the cited pages. 10) c50: the 'symptoms, examination, history' wording came from a Worcestershire Acute Hospitals NHS Trust leaflet, not the cited NHS page, so the citation was corrected and the leaflet added. 11) The final search for a StatPearls statement that a pelvic X-ray is the first test returned only other NCBI-hosted papers, so 'X-ray' was removed from the Investigation key fact. 12) References: StatPearls Sacroiliac Joint, StatPearls Internal Iliac Arteries and the Worcestershire leaflet were added; all 21 original references are still cited. 13) 'Clinical relevance' was split into 'Pelvic and hip fractures' and 'Pelvic girdle pain in pregnancy'; c39 and c41 were supported but removed as duplicates of the intro.
